description: We are a passionate team from Thailand participating in the Bangkok Local Event. We are developing TerraSequence, a decision-support tool utilizing NASA Earth observation data and local agricultural information to optimize sustainable crop rotation, improve soil health, and support climate-resilient farming.
summary: AstroAgri is a satellite-backed, data-driven decision-support platform designed to empower smallholder farmers, agricultural cooperatives, and sustainable farming organizations to adopt resilient crop rotation strategies. Facing unpredictable climate shifts, erratic rainfall, and severe soil degradation from continuous monoculture, farmers often lack actionable insights to select optimal crops. AstroAgri bridges this gap by integrating multi-source NASA Earth observation datasets—including NASA GPM IMERG (10 km daily rainfall), NASA SMAP (soil moisture), and NASA POWER (2001–2025 climatology)—alongside local soil conditions and FAO ECOCROP crop requirements. Through an intuitive mobile interface featuring interactive plot setup, satellite data tracking, 3-year outcome simulation, and a task calendar with 7-day weather forecasts, AstroAgri generates ranked crop rotation plans. Simulations demonstrate potential water savings of up to 28% and an 11% increase in crop yield while restoring long-term soil health.
details:
1. The Problem & Target Impact Continuous monoculture and improper crop rotation deplete soil nutrients and waste water resources, while erratic rainfall and shifting land surface temperatures render traditional farming calendars ineffective. Over 33% of global soils are degraded. AstroAgri supports smallholder farmers (such as those transitioning away from continuous maize cultivation), agricultural cooperatives, and sustainable farming organizations by providing localized, science-backed crop rotation guidance.

2. Technical Architecture & NASA Data Integration AstroAgri connects an intuitive mobile/web user interface to a backend serverless architecture (api/nasa.js hosted on Vercel) that queries NASA's public Common Metadata Repository (CMR) and NASA Earthdata Cloud OPeNDAP using secure server-side authentication and 6-hour location caching

NASA GPM (Global Precipitation Measurement - IMERG): Fetches the last 30 days of daily satellite rainfall observations at a fine 0.1° (~10 km) grid resolution. This real-time 30-day rainfall total feeds directly into our decision engine to classify plot conditions (dry, normal, or wet) and adjust crop rotation match scores.

NASA SMAP (Soil Moisture Active Passive): Retrieves satellite-derived topsoil moisture levels via the same serverless pipeline to assess root-zone water availability.

NASA POWER Climatology (2001–2025): Provides long-term historical rainfall and temperature baselines to cross-check each crop's FAO ECOCROP optimal rainfall range, and acts as an automated fallback source to ensure uninterrupted system reliability.

3. Core Platform Features

  • Plot Setup & Customization: Farmers draw their field boundaries on an interactive map, input soil parameters and crop history, and customize units, languages, and severe weather/soil health alerts.
  • 4. Tools, Coding & Resources Used
  • Datasets: NASA GPM IMERG, NASA SMAP, NASA POWER, NASA Land Surface Temperature (LST), FAO ECOCROP, and Open-Meteo.
